evidence_set: Thirty-one case reports describe 35 people aged 15–53, 5 of them women, who reached hospital with cardiovascular episodes during or soon after cannabis use, most with chest pain, rhythm problems or clots in the heart arteries; use was not always confirmed by testing; 24 had no evidence of coronary artery disease, 18 had a heart attack confirmed by creatine kinase or troponin, and there were 5 strokes or transient ischaemic attacks secondary to a cardiovascular event, 3 possible Brugada syndromes and 1 myocarditis.

Relayed epidemiological studies: case-crossover study of 3882 people with acute myocardial infarction, risk 4.8 (95% CI 2.9–9.5) within 1 h of smoking cannabis and 1.7 (0.6–5.1) within 2 h, without toxicology; cohort of 1913 people after a heart attack, mortality hazard ratio 4.2 (1.2–14) for weekly use and 2.5 (0.9–7.3) for less than weekly use; 3886 people followed 18 years, mortality 29% higher with cannabis use, not significant; national inpatient data, ischaemic stroke adjusted risk ratio 1.17 (1.15–1.20); 2097 people with a heart attack before age 51, cardiovascular mortality adjusted hazard ratio 2.22 (printed as a 90% CI, 1.27–3.70); CARDIA, 5113 young adults followed over 25 years, no association with cardiovascular mortality; French national drug-monitoring reports, 2006–10, 35 cannabis-related notifications about the heart or blood vessels, with 9 deaths.
